subject: dwarfRifleman
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf rifleman with braided beard and blunderbuss.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact but detailed dwarf rifleman model, aiming for roughly 400 lines, with a stocky Warcraft-style build, braided beard, blunderbuss, and skeleton starting with hips around y=0.62.

Still building the skeleton...

Naming the leg chain joints per side with hip as parent, then adding boots as axis-aligned boxes attached to the ankle bone, with a cuff cylinder and toe cap sphere, making sure the foot sits flush at ground level.

Now I'm working out the leg targets relative to boot height, checking leg segment lengths against hip-to-target distance to ensure natural bending. For arms, I'm deciding on a rest pose for the rifleman character — leaning toward arms angled outward and slightly forward-down rather than actively gripping the blunderbuss, to keep the neutral pose readable while still suggesting the character's identity.

Defining the arm joint chain with bend directions, adding a pauldron sphere at the shoulder, and simplifying hands to a fist shape with a thumb capsule for grip. Now I'm setting up the gun geometry in model space, positioned for the right hand to hold.

Still shaping the barrel profile...

For the head, I'm placing a skull sphere scaled wide and flat on the head bone, adding a prominent nose sphere, then planning ruddy mottled skin paint with decal-based eyes.

Still building the character rig...

I'll switch to plain computed points for the braid instead, building sphere parts with explicit bone and position, alternating slight sideways offsets for a plaited look, finished with a gold ring and tassel. For the mustache I'm sweeping curved paths from nose to sides that flare upward at the tips, and I'll add a subtle jaw box beneath since the beard mostly hides the mouth.

Now I'm adding small pointed ears as spheres at the sides of the head, then working on a bronze-steel helmet using a lathed dome profile with a rim and small top spike, positioned above the brow so the face stays the visual focus.

Good enough coverage there. I'll skip wings and feather plumes, keeping it simple with just a brass spike and two small side bolts on the helmet. For the torso, I'm adding leather vest paint and a draped bandolier strap running from shoulder to hip, with small cylindrical cartridges placed along the path as separate parts rather than tangent-aligned sticks.

Still writing attachment logic...

Adding the belt with a gold buckle positioned at the front, and planning extra details like a backpack pouch, a powder horn hanging from the hip, and bronze pauldrons shaped from scaled spheres at the shoulders.

I'll pull metal materials for bronze, steel, and brass from the clockwork kit rather than glow effects, keeping embellishments minimal. For textures, I'm planning at least five: an eye motif, plaid cloth for the kilt, and an emblem crest on the tabard.

Working out the tabard placement, I'm positioning it as a textured front panel hanging from the hips bone, figuring out the body's loft dimensions to place it just in front of the belly without clipping through the torso geometry.

Now I'm sketching out texture functions: mottled skin tones, grain patterns for hair and leather, boot paint, with minimal pose variation before writing the actual color constants and generating the figure code.

Working out proportions next: neck-to-head height, total dwarf height around 1.4-1.5m including helmet, and setting up the head joint position relative to the neck chain, figuring out direction vectors for forward-facing orientation.

Now I'm placing the eyes and nose on the skull surface — computing hit points via local forward/up offsets, deciding symmetry (left eye at positive X doesn't need mirroring), and positioning the nose slightly forward and up from head center.

Still positioning facial features...

Now I'm lofting the beard shape from the jaw down over the chest using stacked stations with varying width and depth, tapering toward the bottom, and considering adding a spike for a pointed beard tip.

Next I'm adding side braids coming off the beard with linked segments, gold rings, and tassel ends, then moving into helmet detailing and torso coloring, choosing a blue tunic with bronze armor accents using mottled textures for the tunic and leather vest, plus a bronze breastplate overlay.

I'll drape the bandolier over the cuirass surface instead of under it, with a belt at the torso and the cuirass positioned to slightly overlap the torso loft for a proper armored look. Then I'll add a neck gorget as a bronze collar ring, and place a decal emblem — maybe crossed tools or a mountain symbol — on the chest front of the cuirass.

For textures I'm settling on four: eyes, the emblem decal, a plaid pattern for a tabard, and a belt buckle detail. I'll skip extra glow effects and keep it simple, hanging the tabard from the hip area down past the belt line so it drapes naturally over the lower body.

Now I'm checking body proportions—belly curve, tabard depth, thigh radius, and belt placement—to make sure everything intersects cleanly without visible gaps. Then I'm working out the right-hand gun placement by calculating the distance between shoulder and hand target coordinates.

Still building arm geometry...

Now I'm working out hand and finger shapes—a fist sphere for the right grip, an open palm with four finger capsules and a thumb for the left—then starting to lay out the gun model with a grip and stock positioned relative to the right hand.

Defining gun hardware...

Adding a simplified disc outline for the bell, then a brass muzzle flare torus at the barrel tip. For the backpack, I'm planning a box plus bedroll cylinder attached near the spine tip joint, figuring out how to reference the spine chain's last joint for attachment.

Next I'm wiring up the parenting: arms off the spine tip, legs off the hips, and a torso loft bone list spanning spine to hips. Then I sketch a powder horn hanging off the left hip using a curved sweep with tapering radius and a brass cap sphere, parented to the hips bone.

For the cartridge bandolier, I'm draping a path diagonally across the chest from the left shoulder to the right hip, clamping it onto the cuirass surface, then sweeping leather geometry along that drape with cylindrical cartridges stuck at even intervals along the path.

Now I'm designing the texture SVGs: dwarf eyes with blue irises and dark eyelid lines in an almond shape, and a gold-ringed emblem with crossed hammer and rifle on a dark blue circular backdrop.

Finalizing details like plaid stripe textures with gold trim and fringe, skipping extra pauldron/helmet decorations, and adding spherical ears with a hair capsule connecting sideburns to the beard for a cohesive look. I'm also setting the leg pants to a brown paint color.

Adding bronze knee pad spheres positioned at the knee joint, then working out the joint naming scheme—three names for a two-span leg means the tip joint lands on the ankle, confirming leg.tip resolves to joints[2].

I'm now building the hip-to-spine chain using a "spine" role, with three path points giving two spans plus a chest tip, and starting the neck segment where the spine ends around y=1.05.

Then I'm adding a jaw joint parented to the head, aimed forward, with the lower jaw partly hidden by a beard loft starting around y=1.21 while the skull covers the rest. Next I'm pulling together the metal paint materials from the kit.

Now I'm working out fine details like the shoulder pauldron: a scaled sphere plus a gold trim torus ring and spike, positioned at the shoulder joint in model coordinates and bound to the arm's first bone, with rest-pose shoulder placement matching the torso's half-width. I'm setting up small helper functions for placing parts and spheres to keep the part-building code concise.

Writing helmet details...

Now I'm working out the cuirass decal surface targeting, then setting up a textured tabard box positioned at the hips with belt-aligned dimensions. I'm also laying out the left hand's finger capsules hanging from the wrist bone, spacing them along the z-axis.
